reviews.outcome: The single-cone avoidance theorem follows directly from two basis theorems already explained in the corpus: if C is not below K, choose a low path; otherwise use a hyperimmune-free path and downward closure to avoid the noncomputable Delta2 target C. This justifies a short extension of hyperimmune-free-basis-theorem. The stronger simultaneous countably-many-cones statement requires a separate construction and is not adopted. No defect found in the selected dichotomy.

reviews.outcome: For each prescribed noncomputable target C, choose a low path if C is not below ordinary halting, and a hyperimmune-free path otherwise. Downward closure and the nonzero Delta2 hyperimmune theorem give avoidance in the latter case. Existing exact same-path conversions transfer the result to effectively closed classes and co-c.e. binary trees. No uniform selector or simultaneous countably-many-cones theorem is asserted. No new source defect found.
